newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: NATO proposes big conventional arms cuts.
newsitem.headline: NATO proposes big conventional arms cuts.

text.p: NATO put forward a proposal at conventional arms reduction talks in Vienna on Thursday aimed at sweetening the alliance's planned eastward expansion for its main opponent Russia.

"The alliance is prepared to take significant steps in this regard. Specifically, the total of future aggregate national ceilings of ground treaty limited equipment of (NATO's) 16 members will be significantly less under the adapted treaty," said the proposal, delivered to the body dealing with the treaty on Conventional Forces in Europe.

"That is the key political signal of this proposal that the alliance is prepared to lower its overall force levels. We see this as unilateral steps. We say significantly so we are not talking about one or two percent here," a western diplomat who attended the meeting said.

A working group will begin discussing NATO's proposals on Tuesday. Officials say the new conventional arms reduction proposal, which modifies the 1990 Conventional Forces in Europe treaty, should go a long way to calming Moscow's fears that NATO could pile up weapons on Russia's borders.

The Russians want a legally binding contract providing security guarantees. The Americans say the proposed modification of CFE, which is a treaty requiring ratification by 30 signatory states, amounts to that legally binding document.

The proposal also establishes a "sensitive geographic region" in central Europe comprising the Baltic enclave of Kaliningrad, Ukraine, Slovakia, Belarus, the Czech Republic, Hungary and Poland. It makes clear that ground equipment in that area cannot increase, officials say.
